newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam draws line on media coverage of banking.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam draws line on media coverage of banking.

text.p: Vietnam, facing growing problems in its domestic banking system, outlined on Wednesday a list of banking topics which it said were barred or restricted from press coverage under state secrecy laws.

The list was accompanied by a directive setting out rules which it said were necessary to maintain the reputation and prestige of the national economy and banking system. It was not clear whether the regulations applied to foreign media.
Included among the list of topics ruled off-limits were documents containing information about promotions or disciplinary actions against banking officials, which had not been cleared for publication
Work of the banking inspectorate, personnel files on key banking officials, and complaints which were under investigation but had not been authorised for media release were also included in the list.

Details of widespread loans problems in Vietnam's national banking system have emerged in both the foreign and domestic media in recent weeks following revelations of overdue payments involving letters of credit.
Vietnam's domestic media operates under strict state controls. A draft banking law is expected to be discussed next month during the spring session of Vietnam's National Assembly.
